source: Each organisation's rulebooks, with the CCPA Guidelines for Prevention of Misleading Advertisement in Coaching Sector, 2024 for coaching ads

rulebooks.name: Brand kit
rulebooks.about: Registered name, helpline, logo, colours and tone of voice, plus readable text and alt text.

rulebooks.name: Branch contact details
rulebooks.about: Phone numbers and addresses on a poster must be the branch's own or the helpline.

rulebooks.name: Honest claims
rulebooks.about: Blocks promised results such as “100% selection” or “guaranteed job”, in English, Hindi and Bengali, and flags disguised ones.

rulebooks.name: People and consent
rulebooks.about: Everyone who appears on a poster, with their signed consent and the channels it covers.

rulebooks.name: Copyright and asset permissions
rulebooks.about: No stock-photo watermarks, and other organisations' names and logos only when head office has approved them.

rulebooks.name: Offerings and prices
rulebooks.about: What you sell, with its approved price and, where it applies, its duration. Checked whenever a poster names one or shows a price.

rulebooks.name: Approved figures
rulebooks.about: Statistics you are allowed to quote, such as results or people served. Checked whenever a poster quotes a figure.

rulebooks.name: Dates, deadlines and availability
rulebooks.about: Dates must exist, match their weekday, and not have passed. Checked whenever a poster shows a date.

rulebooks.name: Offers, discounts and terms
rulebooks.about: Discounts, scholarships and limited-time deals must say how long they last, point to their conditions, and add up.

rulebooks.name: Legal and regulatory compliance
rulebooks.about: The disclaimers head office requires on every poster, and no claims your industry may never make.

rulebooks.name: Exam results (coaching ads)
rulebooks.about: For coaching institutes in India: ranks must match the register, and each topper needs their course, its duration and paid or free beside them (CCPA, 2024).

rules.name: No banned claims
rules.reason: Promising a result nobody can guarantee, such as selection, a rank or a job, misleads readers. India's guidelines on misleading advertisements forbid it.

rules.name: Everyone shown has consent on file
rules.reason: A person's name, photo or story can be used in an ad only with their written consent.

rules.name: Consent is valid
rules.reason: Consent must cover the channel the poster is for, still be in date, and be signed by a guardian if the person is a minor. Consent to use a result must be given after the result.

rules.name: Rank matches the register
rules.reason: Showing a different rank from the one the student earned misleads students and parents.

rules.name: Required details next to each topper
rules.reason: Next to each successful student, the ad must show their rank, the course they took, its duration and whether it was paid or free, so readers know what actually produced the result.

rules.name: Figures match approved figures
rules.reason: Success and impact figures must be true and verifiable. Only figures head office has approved can be used.

rules.name: Offerings named as approved
rules.reason: Courses, products and services must be named, and timed where that applies, exactly as head office approved them.

rules.name: Prices match approved prices
rules.reason: A price on a poster is an offer. It must match the approved price.

rules.name: Branch contact details
rules.reason: A wrong number or address sends enquiries to the wrong place, or to someone who isn't us.

rules.name: No expired prices or figures
rules.reason: Prices and figures are approved for a period. After that they must be re-approved before use.

rules.name: Logo present
rules.reason: Every poster carries the organisation's logo, so readers know who published it.

rules.name: Colours within palette
rules.reason: Large areas of off-brand colour make a branch poster look unofficial.

rules.name: Registered name and helpline present
rules.reason: The registered company name and the helpline tell readers who is responsible for the ad and how to reach head office.

rules.name: Tone of voice
rules.reason: Each organisation describes its tone of voice in the brand kit. The AI flags wording that doesn't fit it; a person decides.

rules.name: Text contrast (4.5:1, large text 3:1)
rules.reason: Low-contrast text is hard to read on phones in sunlight and for people with low vision. WCAG asks for 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.

rules.name: Alt text on social posts
rules.reason: Screen-reader users need a text description of image posts on Instagram and WhatsApp.

rules.name: Disguised guarantees
rules.reason: Phrases like 'selection pakka' or 'seat confirmed' promise a result without saying 'guarantee'. The AI flags them; a person decides.

rules.name: Dates are real dates
rules.reason: A date that doesn't exist, like 31 February, sends people to the wrong day and makes the poster look careless.

rules.name: Day matches the date
rules.reason: When the weekday and the date disagree, readers can't tell which one is right.

rules.name: No deadlines that have passed
rules.reason: A poster whose last date or start date has passed invites people to something they can no longer join.

rules.name: Offers say how long they last
rules.reason: A discount or scholarship with no end date can be claimed long after it was meant to stop.

rules.name: Offers point to their conditions
rules.reason: Readers must be able to find who qualifies and what's excluded before they rely on an offer.

rules.name: Discounts add up
rules.reason: If the percentage doesn't match the prices shown, the offer misleads, whichever number is right.

rules.name: No stock-photo watermarks
rules.reason: A watermark means the image is an unpaid preview. Publishing it breaks the stock library's licence.

rules.name: Other organisations are approved partners
rules.reason: Showing a partner's, sponsor's or university's name or logo needs their permission. Head office lists approved partners in the brand kit.

rules.name: Required disclaimers are present
rules.reason: Head office lists the disclaimers every poster must carry. A missing one can make an ad unlawful.

rules.name: No claims your industry forbids
rules.reason: Some industries have claims they may never make, such as guaranteed returns in finance or a guaranteed cure in healthcare.

reader_checks.name: Poster could be read
reader_checks.reason: If the reader couldn't read the poster, nothing on it was checked. A person must look at it.

reader_checks.name: Key numbers read twice
reader_checks.reason: Ranks, fees, phone numbers and figures are read by two separate readers. When they disagree, a person confirms the right number.

reader_checks.name: People shown are identified
reader_checks.reason: Pramaan doesn't recognise faces. Staff tag the people shown; anyone untagged or uncertain goes to a reviewer.
